title: Make PoseRotationResolver branch rotation deterministic (no first-child dependency)
description:
## Summary

`PoseRotationResolver.Resolve` derives a non-terminal bone's rotation from the direction to `children[0]` — the first child in skeleton order (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Animation/Ik/PoseRotationResolver.cs:39-47). For a branched parent with children A and B, reordering A/B changes the parent's derived pose rotation. This hidden data-order dependency makes the pose contract non-deterministic and unsuitable as an animation hot path.

Source: docs/audits/creaturecreator-latest-main-audit-26-09-05-01-40-00.md, F-03. Fixed point 20392e2; re-verified at HEAD 2a89605 (still children[0], unresolved).

## Scope

- Segment bones derive direction from their own `EndPosition` (segment endpoint), not from an arbitrary first child.
- Terminal joint nodes (no segment) keep rest rotation unless an explicit orientation is part of the pose model.
- Do not use `FindFirstChild` / `children[0]` as a general animation contract.
- If branched-node orientation needs a semantic primary child, make that rule explicit and deterministic.
- Pure math only; no scene, editor, or mutable-generated-state dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A branched-skeleton regression proves the parent's derived rotation does not change when child list order changes.
- Segment bones use their own segment endpoint for direction.
- Terminal joint nodes keep rest rotation.
- Existing rest-pose and unknown-ID coverage stays green.

## Validation

- Focused `PoseRotationResolver` runtime tests (branching-order regression + existing rig/pose suite).
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj` and `ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj` pass 0 errors/warnings.
- Unity PlayMode focused rig/pose run green.

## Findings

- F-03 confirmed at HEAD: PoseRotationResolver.cs:46 uses `pose.GetPosition(children[0])`. Peer review confirms no existing coverage.

## Blockers

- None identified. Related to TSK-0073 (CC-069 rig/pose) and CC-073 geometry binding foundation.

## Next Step

- Implement segment/terminal rotation semantics and add the branching-order regression; validate with the focused PlayMode suite.
